mainEntity.name: How often should implant crowns be professionally maintained?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most dental professionals recommend maintenance visits every six months, similar to natural teeth. However, some patients may benefit from more frequent visits, particularly during the first year after crown placement. Your dental team will recommend an appropriate schedule based on your individual oral health needs and crown design.

mainEntity.name: Can screw-retained crowns become loose over time?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, the retaining screw in screw-retained crowns can occasionally loosen due to normal chewing forces. This is typically a minor issue that can be resolved by tightening the screw during a routine appointment. Regular check-ups help identify and address loose screws before they cause complications.

mainEntity.name: Do implant crowns stain like natural teeth?

acceptedAnswer.text: High-quality ceramic crowns resist staining better than natural teeth, maintaining their appearance longer. However, they can still accumulate surface deposits that may affect their appearance. Professional cleaning and polishing during maintenance visits help preserve crown aesthetics throughout their lifespan.

mainEntity.name: What happens if an implant crown breaks or chips?

acceptedAnswer.text: Treatment depends on the extent of damage and crown type. Minor chips in ceramic crowns can sometimes be polished smooth, whilst larger damages may require crown replacement. Screw-retained crowns can typically be removed easily for repair or replacement, whilst cement-retained crowns may require more complex procedures.

mainEntity.name: Are there special toothpastes for implant crown maintenance?

acceptedAnswer.text: Low-abrasive toothpastes are generally recommended for implant crown maintenance to prevent surface scratching. Some manufacturers produce implant-specific toothpastes, though high-quality, gentle formulations typically provide adequate cleaning without damaging crown materials.

mainEntity.name: How long do different implant crown designs typically last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Well-maintained implant crowns can last 10-15 years or longer, regardless of design type. Longevity depends more on maintenance quality, individual oral health, and lifestyle factors than on the specific crown design. Regular professional care helps maximise crown lifespan for all design types.
